subject: EdgeYard private cluster provisioning: node mapping, storage and retention agreement
messages:
From: Carlos Mendez <carlos.m@tiltworks.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Jul 2028 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: EdgeYard: site inventory + constraints for private cluster provisioning

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier. Attached is the environment spreadsheet and a short inventory (tiltworks-env-specs.pdf) with rack power, available top-of-rack switches, and our expected node footprint. High level constraints:

- Air-gapped room with a single cross-connect to our colo provider.
- No public IPs on worker nodes (NAT for egress only).
- We need data residency inside us-west-2.
- Primary workload: low-latency model inference (1–4ms per token) and batch offline embedding jobs.

Questions for your team before we lock sizes:
1) Recommended node mix for mixed bursty inference + nightly batch?
2) PV strategy: local NVMe for KV/cache, and replicated block store for model artifacts — any pitfalls?
3) Encryption: we have a KMS appliance; can you integrate with customer KMS/HSM for disk encryption keys?

We'd like a draft MOP and a minimal-viable retention policy for persisted model artifacts. Can you propose a mapping by next Tuesday (24 Jul)?

Regards,
Carlos
Ops Lead, TiltWorks
(attachment: tiltworks-env-specs.pdf - PDF)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Mendez <carlos.m@tiltworks.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Jul 2028 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: EdgeYard: site inventory + constraints for private cluster provisioning

Carlos —

Appreciate the context and the attachment. High level answers and a proposed starting point below; we'll follow up with a one-hour sizing call to validate the assumptions.

Summary recommendations (starter):
- Cluster footprint: 6 control-plane (3 masters + 3 standby small VMs for HA), 12 GPU inference workers (A100 or H200 equivalent) spread across 3 racks for failure domain separation, and 6 CPU-heavy batch workers with 512GB RAM for embedding jobs.
- Node roles:
  - inference-gpu: GPU pinned, isolated QoS class, local NVMe for KV cache (ephemeral)
  - model-store-block: small set of nodes attached to high-IOPS encrypted block store (replicated across two racks) for model artifacts
  - batch-cpu: burstable compute for offline jobs; use node taints/tolerations for scheduling
- Storage plan:
  - Local NVMe per GPU node for KV/prefix cache (fast, ephemeral).
  - Replicated block store (iSCSI/Ceph RBD/managed block equivalent) mounted via CSI for persistent model artifacts and serialized checkpoints.
  - Retention: default artifact TTL = 30 days; keep last three model releases as minimum.
- KMS/HSM: yes, we support customer KMS integrations (KMIP/HSM + cloud KMS connectors). We'll map envelope keys so the HSM performs master key ops while Redwood bundles CEKs per-cluster.
- Networking:
  - Private VPC with NAT egress, restricted egress allowlist for model telemetry endpoints.
  - BGP route leaking to colo where required; avoid public worker IPs as requested.

Open questions for TiltWorks:
- Desired RTO/RPO for model artifact restore? (affects replica count and cross-rack sync frequency)
- Will you accept eventual consistency for model catalogs during rolling updates?

Next steps:
- I'll circulate a concise MOP and node-mapping doc by Mon (24 Jul) — draft will include explicit failure-domain diagrams, CSI choices, and a proposed KMS integration sketch.

Cheers,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Private Deployments | Redwood Inference
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Jul 2028 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: EdgeYard: site inventory + constraints for private cluster provisioning

Karthik / Marissa —

Following Karthik's proposed starter, I'm attaching a short draft MOP (draft-mop-v1.md) that we can send to TiltWorks after we confirm a few items. I pulled out operational checkboxes we should validate on the call. Key additions:

- KMS integration details: we need the KMS vendor, KMIP endpoint, and whether HSM is reachable from customer network or proxy. We must list key rotation cadence and who owns rotation.
- Audit & evidence: capture path for audit logs (pod-level stdout/stderr retention and control-plane audit logs pushed to customer SIEM); retention defaults and export process.
- Backup cadence for model-store-block: snapshot cadence, concurrency limits for restore, and dry-run restore window.
- Canary policy: automatic fallback to CPU-only variant when GPU pool is unhealthy, plus throttled traffic shift (10/30/50% steps).
- Service accounts & workload identity: prefer OIDC federated identity to avoid long-lived keys; need TiltWorks to confirm IdP metadata.

Attachments: draft-mop-v1.md (internal MOP) — this contains recommended runbook steps, required preflight checks, and a minimal ops play for restore. Please review the MOP bullets below before I send to Carlos:

- Preflight: rack-level power test, NIC bonding, KMS handshake, vSwitch VLANs, egress allowlist test to our telemetry endpoint.
- Provision: kubeadm / curated distro choice, CSI driver install, CA bootstrap + KMS envelope key handshake.
- Post-provision: smoke inference test, KV-cache warmup, rollback test for model load.

If everyone is OK, I'll send the MOP to Carlos with a proposed Wed 26 Jul 10:00 AM PT call to go line-by-line.

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
(attachment: draft-mop-v1.md - Markdown)

- IdP: we can provide OIDC metadata and run a handshake during the preflight — I'll get that to you by EOD.

We can do Wed 26 Jul 10:00 AM PT for the call. I'll upload the network wiring diagram to our shared drive and send a short Invite.

Thanks — please include the canary policy text in the emailed MOP.

Carlos
